1.descriptions: The BRIAR dataset (via BRIAR Government Collections 1 and 2) is collected and curated to support research on biometric person recognition under extremely challenging, uncontrolled full-motion video conditions—specifically face and whole-body (WB) recognition at long ranges and elevated viewing angles. The dataset includes more than 350,000 still images and over 1,300 hours of video footage of approximately 1,000 subjects, captured using multiple camera types (indoor close-range, mid-range zoom, specialized long-range systems, and UAV platforms) to cover distances up to 1,000 m and elevation/view angles up to 50°. Media are organized into research and test sets; raw recordings are segmented so each final video contains one subject, one clothing set, and one activity, with an emphasis on cross-clothing matching (subjects perform activities in two different clothing sets). Annotations include non-rotated bounding boxes for face and whole-body plus head yaw and pitch angles (generated using YOLOv5 and InsightFace, with additional 3D landmark generation and other post-processing), and video metadata including XML-formatted sensor and environmental information; manual annotation is used to verify/complete difficult frames.

101.descriptions: Objaverse 1.0 (OBJAVERSE) is a large-scale corpus of richly annotated 3D objects intended to provide a foundation for training and evaluating 3D computer vision and multimodal AI models. 103.descriptions: VIPBench is an identity-centric benchmark introduced to evaluate personalized, identity-aware deepfake detection. 109.descriptions: CrossFaceID is a large-scale, high-quality, publicly available dataset intended to improve facial modification capabilities for FaceID customization models by providing controlled input–output facial variations of the same person. During training, a face image of a person is used as input while the model is forced to generate another image of the same person with altered facial features guided by the text description, enabling FaceID personalization and modification while preserving identity.
